_meta.title: Associates link register (owner-supplied tracking ID)
_meta.purpose: One machine-readable record of the Associates ID the owner supplied and the exact published rule that every product link must carry it. tools/attach_associates_tag.py reads this file; nothing is hard-coded in the generator.
tools_that_enforce_it: tools/publish.py (runs it after every builder, then checks it)

tag.supplied_by: Owner, in the session tasking brief
tag.shape: XXXXX-## pattern named in Program Policies Participation Requirements 2(b)
tag.shape_match: The value matches the XXXXX-## shape quoted in the rule below. This is a string-shape observation only.
tag.account_assignment: NOT verified. No Associates account, login, report or Partners Central flow was accessed in this build. A tag that is syntactically correct is not proof that it is assigned to an enrolled, in-good-standing account.

rule.title: Associates Program Policies, including the Associates Program Participation Requirements

clauses.heading: Participation Requirements - 2. Links on Your Site - (a) Special Links
clauses.verbatim: Special Links must use the Associates ID we have assigned to you.
clauses.what_it_requires_here: A product link without the Associates ID is not a Special Link under this clause.

clauses.heading: Participation Requirements - 2. Links on Your Site - (b) General Requirements Applicable to All Special Links
clauses.verbatim: All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site. For example, you must include your Associates ID or “tag” (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.
clauses.what_it_requires_here: Every link this site places to an Amazon product page carries ?tag=<Associates ID>. The rule is quoted, not paraphrased, because the earlier build's opposite rule was written from paraphrase.

clauses.heading: Disqualification for malformed or obscured links
clauses.verbatim: Purchases that are not correctly tracked because links are not properly formatted are disqualified. You will not cloak, hide, spoof, or otherwise obscure the URL of your Site containing Special Links (including by use of Redirecting Links). You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site.
clauses.what_it_requires_here: The public buy button names its Amazon destination and points at the product page directly, with the tag in the URL. The supplied link.amazon short links are the subject of FLG-003 and are not described as invalid; they are simply no longer the destination of a buy button.

tagged.rule: An <a href> whose host is www.amazon.com or amazon.com and whose path contains /dp/<ASIN> or /gp/product/<ASIN>, including product-slug paths such as /Ninja-Capacity-Dehydrate-Technology-AF141/dp/B0CSZ7WBYW.
tagged.why: These are the links a reader can act on: they land on a purchasable product page.

not_tagged.what: The five submitted link.amazon short links
not_tagged.why: Their exact compliance status is unresolved (FLG-003) and the brief says not to call them invalid. They are kept as the observed record of what was submitted. They are no longer the destination of any buy button.

A 9-character token is not an ASIN (Creators API GetItems, ItemIdType=ASIN, requires 10 characters). These links appear only as the evidence of a page-not-found check, and their own text says so. Tagging them would send a reader to an error page under the owner's ID.

not_tagged.what: Amazon browse, search and Best Sellers pages, and Amazon/Associates help, agreement and API documentation pages
not_tagged.why: They are cited sources for a research claim, not product promotions. Tagging a citation would change what the citation is. This boundary is published as an open item for the owner rather than assumed: see 4B0-F-02 on the Flagged for review page.

conflict_rule: If a product link already carries a tag that is not this value, the tool never overwrites it. It leaves the link untouched and reports it, so a foreign tag cannot be silently destroyed.
